model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route): NI to ordinary shareholders less CET1 retention, net debt zero, per ordinary share, USD flows bridged to a GBp quote

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case revenue path average (years 1-10); equity CAGR rejected (see warning); 3yr CAGRs are FY2022 -> FY2025 reported; 5yr CAGRs start from the FY2020 COVID/zero-rate/impairment trough (EPS 10.4c) and overstate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.3-2.6%) diverges by far more than 30% from revenue (7.3-8.7%) and EPS (31-80%) CAGRs. Cause: $9bn+ of buybacks FY2023-FY2025 plus a rising dividend keep parent equity flat (43-47bn since FY2017) while the share count fell 3,325M -> 2,189M and RoTE went from 6.5% to 17.6%; FY2020 is a trough that inflates every 5yr CAGR. Neither series is a forward growth rate; the base case uses management's income guidance (around the middle of 5-7% for 2026) fading to 3% nominal.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are null: bank OCF/FCF is meaningless (deposit and trading-balance flows). SBC is ~1.9% of revenue and stable (1.0-1.9% over FY2017-FY2025, rising with deferred-bonus mix), so the SBC adjustment does not distort growth. EPS is in USD per ordinary share (CSV eps column); the GBp quote is not used in any CAGR.

scenario_narratives.base: Standard Chartered delivers its 2028 RoTE target (~15%) but falls short of the 2030 one (~18%), settling at ~16.5%. Income grows ~5% for three years on Wealth Solutions, Global Markets flow and cross-border network income, with NII flat-to-low-single-digit as AAME policy rates drift down and the balance sheet grows. Costs grow ~2% after the final Fit for Growth charges in 2026, taking cost-to-income from 55-59% toward ~53%. Credit impairment runs ~30bp with Middle East overlays, normalising to ~25-30bp. CET1 is held at ~14% of RWA and roughly 70-85% of NI to ordinary is distributed through the >=30% payout dividend plus $2.5-3bn/yr of buybacks. After 2030 growth fades to 3% nominal.
scenario_narratives.bull: The capital-light re-rating completes. Affluent net new money runs ahead of the $200bn-by-2028 target as Asian and Middle Eastern wealth formation compounds, network income reaches ~70% of CIB, RMB internationalisation and digital-asset services add new fee pools, and the >15% corporate-function headcount reduction drops cost-to-income to ~52%. ECL stays benign at 25-30bp. RoTE hits ~15% in 2028 and ~18% in 2030 as targeted, and sustains at 18.5-19% with revenue growing 5-7% through 2030. Buybacks retire 4-5% of shares a year.
scenario_narratives.bear: The footprint's concentrations bite together. A China/Hong Kong slowdown with tightened offshore-account scrutiny chokes cross-border wealth flows, a wider Middle East conflict and tariff-driven trade contraction push CIB and SME exposures into a credit cycle (ECL ~1% of loans in year 2), and faster USD/HKD rate cuts compress NII. Revenue falls 3% in year 2 and Global Markets/wealth fees shrink with risk appetite. A legacy AML/sanctions matter recurs (the 2012 and 2019 pattern), raising compliance costs. Returns recover only to ~12% RoTE, the FY2024 franchise economics; buybacks pause in the trough year.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Standard Chartered is valued as the cash its ordinary shareholders can actually take out: NI to ordinary (after AT1 and preference coupons and the small NCI) less the CET1 needed to keep the ratio at ~14.2% as risk-weighted assets grow, discounted at an 11.0% USD cost of equity. Deposits are funding, not debt, so net debt is zero and nothing is deducted after the flows. Value is computed per ordinary share in USD and bridged to pence sterling at spot GBPUSD so it is comparable to the LSE quote; the USD siblings are kept alongside. The three scenarios bracket management's May-2026 targets: bear = the FY2024 economics after an EM credit cycle, base = 2028 target met and 2030 target missed, bull = both met on schedule.
key_risks_to_valuation: Emerging-market credit cycle: a China/HK, Middle East or trade-driven ECL spike is the bear case; impairment at ~1% of loans takes ~10pp off the year-2 margin
RoTE path: the base assumes 14.4% -> 16.5%; every 1pp of sustained RoTE is worth roughly 6-7% of value, so the gap between the 15% and 18% targets is the gap between base and bull
NII sensitivity to USD/HKD/SGD rate cuts: NII is 51% of income and guided only to low-single-digit growth
AML/sanctions conduct: a new enforcement action (2012 $667m, 2019 $1.1bn + GBP102m) would hit both the flow and the cost of equity
AT1 coupon drag: the stack grew to $9.1bn in H1'26; coupons of ~$640m/yr are ~12% of NI to ordinary and rise with every issuance
FX: a GBp holder's value moves one-for-one with GBPUSD; a 5% stronger pound takes ~5% off every GBp figure here with no change in the USD business
RWA intensity: base/bull assume RWA grows at 0.8x revenue; if RWA tracks revenue 1:1 the base loses ~5% of value

Share count: the $1.0bn Q3-2026 buyback (~37M shares at current prices) is not deducted because the count is paired with the 30-Jun CET1; a reader comparing to a post-buyback share count should also lower CET1 by ~$1.0bn

sanity_check_caveat.status: EXPECTED FALSE PASS -- scripts/sanity_check.py applies inputs.fx_rate in the quote->reporting direction while dcf_engine.py defines fx_rate as model->quote (USD -> GBp = 75.5687). It will therefore multiply the GBp price by 75.57 instead of dividing, grading a fictitious ~$160,000 share (P/B ~3,700x, P/Sales ~17,000x), as it did on HSBA.L and BA.L. Same systemic bug recorded in memory (sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-systemic-bug); not fixed here because scripts/ changes need TDD + corpus recompute. Do not read the sanity_check block's multiples as real.

real_multiples_at_current_price.basis: price 2,119.0p / 75.5687 = $28.04 per ordinary share; TTM EPS = NI to ordinary 4,861 / weighted basic 2,222 = $2.19; FY2025 reported EPS 195.4c, underlying 229.7c; TNAV/share $17.55 and NAV/share $20.47 at 30-Jun-2026; P/Sales on 2,189M shares and TTM revenue 21,640. P/TNAV 1.6x against a 15-18% RoTE target and 11% CoE is consistent with a justified P/TNAV of (RoTE - g)/(CoE - g) = (15.5-3)/(11-3) = 1.56x, i.e. the market is pricing the 2028 target being met and the 2030 target discounted -- which is the base case.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 1,351.5-2,364.0p; GBPUSD=X for the fx bridge
data_sources.financials: Standard Chartered PLC Annual Reports FY2018-FY2025 and Half Year Report 2026 (research/STAN.L/Extracted), STAN.L_Metrics.csv and kpis (FY2017-FY2025 annual, Q1/H1 FY2025 and FY2026 interims; the H2-2026 files were mislabeled duplicates of H1 and were excluded); Half Year Report 2026 for H1'26 flows, capital, share counts and TNAV
data_sources.qualitative: STAN.L_Analysis.json (2026-10-10), incl. the May-2026 Capital Markets Day targets and H1-2026 guidance upgrade

inputs.share_count_basis: ORDINARY SHARES, fully diluted, millions. 2,189M ordinary shares in issue excluding own shares at 30-Jun-2026 (STAN.L_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:175) plus 65M dilutive potential ordinary shares (H1'26 EPS note: diluted 2,287M vs basic 2,222M weighted, lines 6378-6379) = 2,254M. The $1.0bn buyback announced 31-Jul-2026 (line 756-758, 'commencing imminently', ~38bp of CET1) is NOT deducted: no post-June filing is in Extracted and the count must pair with the 30-Jun CET1 anchor -- 2,189M shares with CET1 14.2% and ~2,152M shares with CET1 ~13.8% are the same equity, so either consistent pair gives the same value per share. Held FLAT thereafter: SBC is expensed inside the flow and buybacks are the distribution of the flow, value-neutral per share.
inputs.sbc_source: TTM to 2026-06-30: FY2025 'Share-based payment costs (Note 31)' 399 (STAN.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:22786) - H1'25 206 + H1'26 216 (STAN.L_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt:6183). Bank: last_fcf is NI to ORDINARY shareholders TTM (FY25 4,558 at Annual_FY2025:3643 - H1'25 3,065 + H1'26 3,368 at HalfYear_H1-2026:144 = 4,861); reported_fcf = NI + SBC for auditability. Equity-award taxes not separately disclosed, nil assumed.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 buybacks: $2,719m cash in financing (kpis ShareRepurchases); $2,800m charged to equity (Annual_FY2025:21874) because the $1.3bn July-2025 programme completed 26-Jan-2026. H1'26: $1,737m cash (kpis), being the $1.5bn Feb-2026 programme (62.8M shares at ~GBP17.8 VWAP, completed 24-Jun-2026, HalfYear_H1-2026:749-752) plus the tail of the prior one. New $1.0bn programme announced 31-Jul-2026. Ordinary dividends paid FY2025 $954m (Annual_FY2025:21955); FY2025 DPS 61c (+65%); 2026 interim DPS 20.4c (+66%, formulaic one-third of prior-year total). Policy: payout >= 30% of earnings plus buybacks, CET1 managed inside 13-14%.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows are USD (Standard Chartered's reporting currency; the share capital is $0.50 ordinary shares); the LSE quote is pence sterling. fx_rate converts model to quote: 1 USD = 100 / GBPUSD 1.3233 = 75.5687 GBp (Yahoo GBPUSD=X, 2026-10-09 21:29 UTC). The engine multiplies every USD per-share figure by it, so canonical intrinsic_value, weighted_iv and entry_price are in GBp and comparable to current_price; *_usd siblings hold the model-currency figures. Same bridge and rate as the HSBA.L build of 2026-10-10. Parity: no NYSE ADR to check against (the US ADR was delisted; 2888.HK trades at HKD but was not fetched). The buyback VWAP of GBP17.8 for 62.8M shares = $1.5bn implies 1 GBP ~ $1.34, consistent with the rate used.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T16:00:08Z LSE regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API; 2026-10-10 is a Saturday, no later print)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 11.0% built in USD because the flows are USD (the GBp quote is bridged at spot, not discounted at a GBP rate): 10y UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.15 x 5.25% ERP = ~10.2%, plus ~0.8pp for the emerging/frontier-market concentration of earnings (Hong Kong, Singapore, India, China, UAE, Africa), the live Middle East conflict overlays, and the AML/sanctions conduct history (2012 and 2019 settlements). Above HSBC/HSBA.L (10.5%: broader, with a UK/HK retail deposit base), level with BCS (11.0%), below nothing in the UK-bank set. One rate across all three scenarios; risk is carried in the bear path and its 25% weight.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: the bank FCFE flow is after all operating costs including occupancy and IFRS-16 depreciation/interest; lease liabilities are operating funding, not deducted.
inputs.nci_treatment: Inside the flow. 'ebitda' = PBT + SBC - pre-tax equivalent of (AT1 and preference coupons + NCI), so the flow is NI to ORDINARY shareholders. TTM AT1/preference dividends 568 (FY25 527 at Annual_FY2025:21873 - H1'25 244 + H1'26 285 at HalfYear_H1-2026:1174); NCI 13 (FY25 12 - 17 + 18). AT1 par rose 7,528 -> 9,105 in H1'26 ($1.6bn net issuance, HalfYear_H1-2026:5107, 5561), so coupons step up to ~$640m/yr from year 1; preference capital 1,494 is constant. AT1, preference capital and NCI are NOT deducted again in a bridge: shareholders_equity in the CSV (46,308) is parent equity INCLUDING the 1,494 preference shares but EXCLUDING the 9,105 AT1 (shown separately) and 480 NCI; tangible ordinary equity = 46,308 - 1,494 - ~6,334 intangibles = ~38,480 = TNAV 1,755c x 2,189M.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE at cost of equity through the component engine with net_debt = 0 -- the house method for large banks (WFC, USB, TFC, HBAN, NAB.AX, HSBC/HSBA.L, LYG, BCS). SKILL.md routes banks to residual income on tangible book; FCFE-at-CoE with a CET1-retention charge is the same economics (value = TCE + PV of returns above CoE) expressed as distributable cash. Deposits ($553bn customer accounts) are operating funding, not debt; OCF is meaningless for a bank (CSV OCF swings -20bn to +37bn), total_debt is NULL in core_metrics by design (debt securities 79bn and subordinated liabilities 8.8bn are funding, held in kpis) and FCF CAGRs are not computed. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = reported operating income (CSV definition); TTM to 2026-06-30 = FY25 20,942 - H1'25 10,906 + H1'26 11,604 = 21,640. 'ebitda' = PBT 7,364 (6,963 - 4,383 + 4,784) + SBC 409 - (AT1/pref 568 + NCI 13) / (1 - 26.1%) 786 = 6,987 = 32.3% of revenue. FY0 check: (6,987 - 409) x (1 - 26.1%) = 4,861 = NI to ordinary. TTM is on the REPORTED basis (the Group dropped 'underlying' reporting from 2026) and carries ~$0.9bn of H2-25 notable items (restructuring 320, Fit for Growth 531, DVA 31, other 55; Annual_FY2025:1265-1268) plus H1'26 Middle East overlays (234, HalfYear_H1-2026:280), so year 1 steps up toward the H1'26 run-rate (H1'26 alone: 39.7% engine margin, 17.6% RoTE) netted against seasonally heavier H2 costs and the final year of FFG charges inside the ~$13.3bn 2026 cost guidance. 'capex' = CET1 retention to hold CET1 at 14.2% of RWA as RWA grows. RWA/revenue has fallen 12.64 (FY24) -> 12.32 (FY25) -> 12.08 (H1'26) as the mix shifts to capital-light Wealth and network income, so base and bull grow RWA at 0.8x revenue growth: retention % of revenue = 0.142 x 12.08 x 0.8 x g/(1+g) = 137.2 x g/(1+g); bear grows RWA 1:1 with revenue (risk-weight inflation in a credit cycle): 171.0 x g/(1+g), floored at zero. CET1 14.2% sits 20bp above the 13-14% target range (~$0.5bn, ~$0.23/share) but the $1.0bn Q3-2026 buyback spends it, so NO excess-capital credit in the bridge. D&A = 0 (inside opex). SBC 1.9% of revenue flat. CoE 11.0% USD. HORIZON: 10 years, year 1 = Jul-2026 to Jun-2027. Sanity_check.py will misapply fx_rate (see sanity_check_caveat).

bear.margin_rationale: An emerging-market credit cycle in year 2: China/Hong Kong slowdown plus a widening Middle East conflict and tariff-driven trade contraction take credit impairment to ~1% of loans (~$3bn vs ~$0.9bn normal, ~10pp of margin), Global Markets and wealth fees fall with risk appetite (revenue -3%), and faster USD/HKD rate cuts compress NII. Recovery only to a 31% margin: terminal RoTE ~12%, the FY2024 underlying economics (11.7%) with partial credit for Fit for Growth. CET1 retention floored at zero in the contraction year (regulators would not permit a capital release in a credit cycle) and RWA tracks revenue 1:1 thereafter (171.0 x g/(1+g)) as risk weights inflate. ETR 27% on less deductibility. Terminal multiple capped at 12x FCFE.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 (Jul-26 to Jun-27) 5.5%: FY2026 income guided around the middle of 5-7% at constant currency (raised at H1'26 from the bottom end; HalfYear_H1-2026 and Analysis guidance block), H1'26 printed +6% (+8% ex the Solv India gain in the H1'25 base), NII guided low-single-digit growth with non-NII (Wealth Solutions, Global Markets, Global Banking) growing double digit. Years 2-3 5.0%: the Capital Markets Day (May 2026) wealth and network-income targets ($200bn affluent NNM by 2028, Wealth Solutions double-digit CAGR) sustain growth above nominal GDP; then fading 4.5 -> 3.0% as rate tailwinds normalise and the franchise grows with AAME nominal GDP.
base.margin_rationale: Year 1 34.8% gives NI to ordinary ~$5.6bn = ~14.4% RoTE on ~$39bn average tangible equity: H1'26 ran 17.6% but H2 carries seasonally heavier costs (FY2026 opex ~$13.3bn flat incl. the final Fit for Growth charges, vs $6.3bn in H1), credit impairment ~30bp of loans with Middle East overlays, and AT1 coupons ~$640m on the enlarged $9.1bn stack. Margin rises to 37.8% by year 4 (2030) as FFG charges end, cost growth is held near 2% against 4.5-5% income growth and the >15% corporate-function headcount cut lands: implied RoTE 15.1% in year 2 (the ~15% 2028 target, met) and ~16.4% in year 4 (the ~18% 2030 target, NOT met in base -- it requires the bull). Terminal 38.0% holds RoTE ~16.5%.
base.capex_rationale: CET1 retention 137.2 x g/(1+g) holding CET1 at 14.2% of RWA with RWA growing at 0.8x revenue (continued capital-light mix shift, RoRWA 8.6% -> 8.8% in H1'26). Implied distribution ratio ~71% of NI to ordinary in year 1 and ~85% at terminal, consistent with the >=30% dividend plus the $2.5-3bn/yr buyback cadence of FY2024-FY2026.
base.tax_rationale: TTM ETR 26.1% (FY25 26.8%, H1'26 23.3%, FY24 32.8%); 25% reflects the downward trend from improved UK profitability (UK losses previously non-relievable), HK 16.5%, Singapore 17%, India ~35%, UK bank surcharge and Pillar Two.

bull.margin_rationale: Management's May-2026 targets are hit on schedule: ~15% RoTE in 2028 and ~18% in 2030, then sustained. Income grows at the top of the 5-7% range (7% year 1 incl. a weaker USD lifting reported numbers) as affluent net new money runs ahead of the $200bn-by-2028 target, Global Markets and network income compound, and NII turns positive on volume. Cost-to-income falls toward ~52% by 2030; ECL stays ~25-30bp. Implied RoTE ~15% year 1, ~17% year 3, ~18.5-19% from year 4. Same CET1 retention rule as base (0.8x RWA tracking); same 11.0% CoE.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (up from the 15% house default): earnings are concentrated in a handful of emerging and frontier markets (Hong Kong, Singapore, India, China, UAE) with live Middle East overlays, China/HK regulatory tightening in 2026, EM FX translation risk and a documented AML/sanctions enforcement history. Base 50%: FY2026 guidance was raised at H1 and the 13% RoTE target was hit a year early. Bull 25% (down from 35%): H1'26 RoTE 17.6% already sits at the 2030 target, so the bull needs peak-cycle returns to persist and improve rather than mean-revert. Same 25/50/25 as HSBC/HSBA.L; LYG used 20/50/30 for a UK-only retail lender without EM exposure.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
